thread:
saumya: Quick heads-up — infra asked for a checklist proving tenant isolation for Private installs. They want answers on netpol default-deny gaps, sidecar access to KMS (customer-managed vs cluster), and audit log exfiltration risk. Can we triage?

jon: Thanks. Do we have a repro that shows an egress path from runtime pods to customer KMS (or to internet) that worry them?

tom: Short answer: sidecar runs in-pod, uses mTLS to KMS over the VPC. Two common deployment modes: (1) customer-managed KMS via private link / endpoint; (2) cluster-managed KMS shim. Which one are they using?

saumya: Legal says customer-controlled keys only — so they pick (1). Their concern: pod -> node -> NAT -> internet. They want netpol proof + KMS policies that bind key usage to network and SA.

maria: For netpol: default-deny for ingress+egress at namespace level, explicit allow only to KMS endpoint CIDRs (or VPC endpoint). Also enforce `hostNetwork: false` and deny privileged containers / hostPath.

dave: +1. And enforce egress via VPC endpoint (no NAT). We can produce VPC flow logs showing no outbound 0.0.0.0/0.

jon: Can someone paste a minimal NetworkPolicy we can include in the attestation?

tom: snippet below:
```
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: deny-egress-except-kms
spec:
  podSelector: {}
  policyTypes:
  - Egress
  egress:
  - to:
    - ipBlock:
        cidr: 10.10.0.0/24 # VPC endpoint for customer KMS
    ports:
    - protocol: TCP
      port: 443
```

maria: Also add an OPA gate to block `hostNetwork: true`, `privileged: true`, and all `hostPath` mounts in pod specs.

saumya: Audit logging question: can runtime send audit stream directly into customer's logging cluster so logs never persist on a third-party bucket? They want "no 3rd-party copy" attestation.

tom: Yes. Runtime supports forwarding over a VPC peering or private link into a customer-managed logging endpoint. We can provide signed delivery receipts for each file.

dave: For the attack surface: if a pod is compromised and tries to call KMS with stolen creds, KMS IAM should have conditions: source VPC, allowed service account ARN, and time-bound keys. We should show a sample IAM condition + test.

maria: Test plan idea: spin a throwaway pod that uses the same service account but runs from a blocked subnet and verify decrypt calls fail. We'll record the failed attempt in the audit stream.

saumya: Can infra run that test and dump flow logs + audit lines? Legal wants a one-page attestation listing controls (netpol, KMS IAM conditions, no hostNetwork, audit forwarding into customer VPC, flow logs retention, quarterly pentest).

jon: I'll draft the attestation and include a short flow-log snippet once infra finishes the test.

maria: I'll draft the KMS IAM condition and the test steps.

saumya: Great. If infra test shows any egress to 0.0.0.0/0 we block releases until fixed.

infra-bot: test-run queued — job id 9876. Will post results to thread when finished.

infra-bot: test-run complete — no outbound observed to 0.0.0.0/0. Flow logs and audit lines: s3://redwood-tests/9876/flowlogs.txt (access controlled).

saumya: Awesome, thanks everyone. I'll assemble the attestation and ping Legal for sign-off.
